description:
Upstream NJOY2016 defect, found 2026-09-15 while closing op-12lu's Case A leg. Recorded because this port deliberately does NOT reproduce it, and a future reader comparing Fe-58 against NJOY will otherwise conclude the port is broken.

THE DEFECT. RECONR's unfac (reconr.f90:4473-4496) is 'if (l.eq.0) ... else if (l.eq.1) ... else if (l.eq.2) ... endif' with no else. For l>=3 it assigns NEITHER of its two output arguments, so vl and ps keep whatever the previous call left in them. csunr1 then applies 'vl = vl*e2' (:4010) INSIDE its j loop, so at l>=3 vl is multiplied by another sqrt(E) for every J-state. PURR's unfac2 (purr.f90:1487-1511) has the identical gap.

NOT SHARED BY UNRESR. uunfac (unresr.f90:1213-1239) writes a bare 'else', clamping l>=2 to the l=2 formula. This crate's penetrability_factor ports uunfac and uses a '_ =>' arm, so it is faithful to its own source. Gated by our_penetrability_clamps_l_at_two_like_uunfac so nobody 'fixes' it toward RECONR.

MEASURED on Fe-58 (ENDF/B-VIII.0 Beta4, MAT 2637, NLS=4, so L=3 exists with 2 J-states). NJOY's MF=2/MT=152 stored total runs 1.422225e4 b at 3.5e5 eV to 6.620656e5 b at 3.0e6 eV -- about 1900x the unitarity limit 4pi/k^2 (~7.5 b at 350 keV) and RISING with energy, which no cross section does there. Ours reads 4.567886e0 and 4.755880e0, tracking the evaluation's own MF=3 MT=1 (4.728395e0 and 3.640540e0) within a factor 2. NJOY exceeds us by 3113x at the bottom of the range and 139210x at the top.

DIAGNOSIS IS MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED. tests/reconr_mt152_case_a_and_lssf1_vs_njoy2016.rs carries reproduce_csunr1_with_upstream_fall_through, which implements csunr1 literally including the fall-through, and lands on NJOY's published totals to 2.68e-7 at every one of the 13 energies. The same test asserts NJOY/ours stays above 100x, so it fails if the port ever starts reproducing the defect.

BLAST RADIUS. Only evaluations with NLS>3 in an LRU=2 range. Fe-58 is the only such case among the tapes held in reference-data/endf/. For LSSF=1 (which Fe-58 is) the values never reach transport: MF=3 carries the cross sections and MT=152 is consumed by UNRESR/PURR only as the denominator of self-shielding ratios, where the scale cancels. An LSSF=0 material with NLS>3 would be the dangerous case -- none is held, and none is known to exist offhand; worth a screen if one turns up.

NOT PATCHED HERE. upstream_source/NJOY2016 is a read-only vendored copy. Deliverable is this record plus the test and the docs in src/reconr/urr.rs and reference-data/reconr/README.md.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
2026-09-15 WRITTEN UP AS GitHub issue #210 (theodoreOnzGit/outram-park-backend), with exact file:line citations on both sides.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS BEAD, both found while checking line numbers for the issue rather than trusting what I had written here:

1. csunr2 HAS THE SAME DEFECT. This bead said the runaway was csunr1's. It is not: csunr2 (Case C, LRF=2) has the identical pattern -- do j=1,njs at reconr.f90:4217, call unfac at :4246, vl=vl*e2 at :4247. So ANY LRU=2 range with NLS>3 is affected, in either representation, not just Case A/B. unfac is called from exactly these two places and nowhere else (csaa at :4385 does not call it).

2. PURR IS WRONG BUT BOUNDED, not equally broken. unfac2 (purr.f90:1487-1511) has the same missing else, but its call site writes gnx=gnox*vl*e2*amun (:1437) WITHOUT reassigning vl, so there is no compounding -- l>=3 just silently reuses the previous J-state's penetrability. Only RECONR's two routines reassign vl inside the J loop and therefore compound. The three-way table is in the issue.

BLAST RADIUS NOW MEASURED, not estimated. Screened every evaluation in reference-data/endf/ through this port's own MF=2 parser and counted L-states per unresolved range: 9 real evaluations carry an LRU=2 range, and exactly ONE reaches NLS>3 -- Fe-58 Beta4 (NLS=4). Everything else stops at NLS<=3 where the defect cannot fire. Crucially the dangerous pairing, NLS>3 AND LSSF=0 (where the inflated table is added straight into MF=3 and would reach transport), is present in NOTHING we hold. Fe-58 is LSSF=1, so its garbage stays in self-shielding ratios where the scale cancels.

FOUR OPEN CONFIRMATION STEPS recorded in the issue, the first two being the maintainer's JANIS suggestion made concrete: (a) check the RELEASED ENDF/B-VIII.0 Fe-58 -- we hold Beta4, a pre-release, so it is not yet established that a shipping library is affected at all; (b) pull a third-party PENDF (JANIS / OECD-NEA) for an NLS>3 material and look at its MT=152, which would rule out anything specific to our gfortran 13.3.0 build -- with the caveat that most distributed processed libraries are major actinides, all NLS<=3, so the search is for a STRUCTURAL material; (c) screen whole libraries for NLS>3 in LRU=2 ranges, turning '1 of 9 tapes we happen to hold' into a real number; (d) read current upstream reconr.f90, since we pin 2016.79 and it may already be fixed.

NOT REPORTED TO njoy/NJOY2016. That repo is not in this session's GitHub scope and nothing was filed there. The issue says the upstream fix is one line -- give unfac and unfac2 the bare else that uunfac (unresr.f90:1231) already has -- and that it is worth reporting only once (a) or (c) shows an LSSF=0 material with NLS>3.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
2026-09-15 TASK A ANSWERED -- THE DEFECT REACHES A SHIPPING LIBRARY. Maintainer supplied the released ENDF/B-VIII.0 Fe-58; the sandbox proxy blocks www-nds.iaea.org (403) so it could not be fetched here. Committed as 6e0cee598, pushed.

THE TAPE ACTUALLY TESTED, from its own MF=1/451: '26-Fe- 58 CIELO EVAL-Oct16 Nobre,Herman,Leal,Trkov,Brown,...', 'NDS 148, 214 (2018) DIST-FEB18', '----ENDF/B-VIII.0 MATERIAL 2637', $Rev 1507 / 2018-02-02. Our existing copy is '----ENDF/B-VIII.beta', EVAL-Mar16, $Rev 1070 / 2017-02-17. Genuinely different files: 9.28 MB against 7.95 MB.

RESULT: the unresolved block is CHARACTER-FOR-CHARACTER IDENTICAL between beta and release. Same 3.5e5..3.0e6 eV, LRU=2/LRF=1/LFW=0/LSSF=1, same NLS=4, same widths on all four L states. The URR was never touched between the two. NJOY therefore produces byte-identical MF=2/MT=152 from both -- 1.422225e4 b at 350 keV to 6.620656e5 b at 3 MeV, ~1900x the unitarity limit, rising with energy.

SO THE 'IT IS ONLY A PRE-RELEASE ARTEFACT' ESCAPE IS CLOSED. Every NJOY-derived PENDF of ENDF/B-VIII.0 Fe-58 carries the inflated table.

SEVERITY UNCHANGED THOUGH, and this matters for how loudly to report it: Fe-58 is LSSF=1, so genunr returns at reconr.f90:1694 and the bad table never enters MF=3. UNRESR/PURR use it only as the denominator of self-shielding ratios where the scale cancels. NO TRANSPORT RESULT IS WRONG because of this, on this nuclide. The combination that would corrupt one is NLS>3 AND LSSF=0, and nothing held here has it.

GATED, not just written down: released_and_beta_fe58_carry_the_same_unresolved_parameters asserts the 13 unresolved records match field by field and that both reach L=3. If a future ENDF release changes those parameters the test fires rather than letting this claim go stale. The released tape is also a fourth case in the grid/flags gate with its own committed oracle.

DROPPED gh:#211 Task C (hunt for a third-party PENDF). Two independently distributed evaluations of the same nuclide, processed here, give output identical to a Rust reimplementation of the defective code path. Nothing left for it to rule out.

NOW THE ONLY QUESTION THAT MATTERS is gh:#211 Task B: does any shipping evaluation trip this with LSSF=0. That is the case that actually corrupts MF=3. Needs whole neutron sublibraries screened, not single nuclides. Maintainer may supply VIII.1 / JEFF-3.3 / JENDL-5 Fe-58 later, but single nuclides only answer 'did other evaluators make the same choice', not the LSSF=0 question.

STILL NOT REPORTED to njoy/NJOY2016 -- out of session scope, and worth doing only after Task D (check whether current upstream already has the else).

Verified: njoy 840 passed / 0 failed / 8 ignored, exit 0.

The cold-helium run drops ~430 pt down the SG-vessel side (circulator discharge

If it should be shorter, the circulator needs to sit lower in the SG vessel, or

maintainer, not a defect.

Needs a human at a screen: the implementing agent could not see the rendered
result.

description:
Maintainer's architecture direction, 2026-08-04:

  'tampines will be an improvement of the turbine from tampines-steam-tables.
   The turbine from tampines-steam-tables should be based on TampinesSteamArray
   (HEM code) which will be the baseline that other solvers will be built on.'

TampinesSteamArray lives at crates/tampines-steam-tables/src/openfoam_algorithms/rhoPimpleFoam/mod.rs:705 -- the homogeneous-equilibrium (HEM) array. It becomes the BASELINE that higher-fidelity solvers are measured against and built on (see the sibling bead for drift-flux / 6-eqn).

Turbine consequence: the turbine model in tampines-steam-tables today is ThreePhaseElectricGeneratorTurbine (steam_turbine_equations/generator.rs) -- a real, working lumped torque balance giving omega, EMF, current and power, but purely electromechanical: it has no steam path. tampines' turbine should improve on it by coupling that rotor to a TampinesSteamArray steam path rather than taking torque as a free input.

Note tampines::components::Turbine (components/turbine.rs:13) is currently inert -- inlet: HemSteamCv + adiabatic_efficiency: Ratio, and expand_to() returns NotYetImplemented. That is the shell this work fills in.

Remember the workspace convention (memory: arrays use (p,h) flash): TampinesSteamArray/OPCPFluidArray default to (p,h) flashing because it carries phase data; (T,p) single-phase flashes panic on two-phase.
title: tampines: TampinesSteamArray (HEM) as the baseline two-phase solver, and the turbine built on it

description:
`outram_mc_libs::rng::lcg::init_seed(id, offset, master_seed)` (crates/outram-mc-libs/src/rng/lcg.rs:90) computes:

    let base = future_seed(DEFAULT_STRIDE, master_seed as u64);
    future_seed((id + offset) as u64, base)

i.e. future_seed(DEFAULT_STRIDE + id + offset, master). Consecutive ids therefore land ONE LCG step apart.

OpenMC's own init_seed (canonical source, /home/teddy0/Documents/research/openmc/src/random_lcg.cpp:60) is:

    return future_seed(static_cast<uint64_t>(id) * prn_stride, master_seed + offset);

i.e. id * STRIDE steps apart. The port drops the multiplication.

IMPACT: any caller using init_seed for per-particle / per-stream separation gets streams that are a one-draw shift of each other rather than independent — the exact opposite of the reproducible-parallel-MC guarantee the doc comment claims ('Each particle gets a unique starting seed by striding from the master seed'). Two particles' histories would be near-perfectly correlated. Needs checking against the actual transport call sites: if init_seed is used to seed particle streams, k-eff statistics may be affected.

FOUND BY: the raffles samplers port (op-vjw.2), which needs independent per-dimension streams for Latin hypercube sampling. raffles works around it by calling future_seed(stream * DEFAULT_STRIDE, master) directly with OpenMC's semantics; the workaround and the discrepancy are documented in crates/raffles/src/samplers.rs (stream_seed) and crates/raffles/CLAUDE.md.

SUGGESTED FIX: future_seed((id + offset) as u64 * DEFAULT_STRIDE, master_seed as u64), plus a regression test asserting that init_seed(k) and init_seed(k+1) are DEFAULT_STRIDE steps apart. Verify against the C++ before changing — the offset placement differs too (OpenMC adds offset to the master seed, this port adds it to the id).

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
FIX IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-06 (uncommitted, awaiting maintainer review — AI output is untrusted draft per RESPONSIBLE_USE.md).

crates/outram-mc-libs/src/rng/lcg.rs now mirrors /home/teddy0/Documents/research/openmc/src/random_lcg.cpp:60-64:

    pub fn init_seed(id: i64, offset: i64, master_seed: i64) -> u64 {
        future_seed(
            (id as u64).wrapping_mul(DEFAULT_STRIDE),
            master_seed.wrapping_add(offset) as u64,
        )
    }

Both defects in this bead are fixed: id now MULTIPLIES the stride (streams 152917 draws apart, not 1), and offset is added to the MASTER SEED (independent run, not a shift within one). Signature kept per the maintainer's instruction; the master_seed parameter is documented as a deliberate deviation from OpenMC's global.

BLAST RADIUS (measured, not assumed): init_seed had ZERO library call sites. Its only users are 5 sites in examples/triso_stochastic_gpu.rs. All library transport code (physics::keff, pebble_beds::keff_delta, physics::transport_csg, gpu::batched_*) already calls future_seed(idx * STRIDE, base) directly with correct OpenMC semantics, so no k-eff or transport statistic was ever produced through the bug.

TESTS: 4 new regression tests in rng::lcg::tests, each verified to FAIL against the old implementation:
  - init_seed_consecutive_ids_are_one_full_stride_apart
  - init_seed_matches_openmc_golden_values (5 golden seeds computed by an independent Python implementation of the upstream recurrence)
  - init_seed_streams_do_not_overlap (old impl: 4095/4095 lag-1 exact matches — stream 1 WAS stream 0 shifted one draw)
  - init_seed_offset_selects_an_independent_run
Suite: 234 -> 238 passing, 0 failed, 0 pre-existing test moved.

RECORDED RESULTS: verification_and_validation/gpu_benchmarks/triso_stochastic_cls_gpu.csv was stale (produced 2026-07-21 through the bug). Re-run 2026-08-06 on an RTX A5000; CSV regenerated and the example's V&V doc block updated with the new measured values plus an explicit supersession note. CPU f64 reference moved 0.7013826 -> 0.7014103 (+0.0000277, 0.04 sigma) — the central value was barely biased; what was invalid was the quoted binomial sigma, since neighbouring histories were not independent samples.

SIBLING DEFECT FOUND, NOT FIXED HERE: rng::lcg::prn omits OpenMC's PCG-RXS-M-XS output permutation -> filed as op-jis (P1). Larger blast radius (all recorded stats + WGSL shaders + raffles), needs its own planned change.
ALSO: 2 pre-existing doctest failures in geometry::surface unrelated to this -> op-keh (P2).

title: outram-mc-libs: init_seed derives streams 1 step apart, not 1 stride apart

description:
Maintainer intent 2026-08-12: the nodalised counter-flow steam generator being built for htgr_sim_v1 is to be reused by fhr_sim_v2.

ARCHITECTURE CONSTRAINT: it cannot live in outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/ -- that crate's CLAUDE.md states its library is PRESENTATION ONLY, 'no new physics'. And duplicating it across two examples would guarantee drift. The correct home is most likely the tampines crate, the central TH framework that already composes tuas / coolprop / tampines-steam-tables.

It is being BUILT inside examples/htgr_sim_v1/physics/ for now, deliberately written so promotion is a file move plus an import fix rather than a rewrite: no crate:: paths back into the example, no dependency on HtgrSnapshot or app/, self-contained public API, and all geometry / UA / metal mass / fluids as constructor parameters rather than constants read from Htr10DesignPoint.

The hot side must not assume helium -- fhr_sim_v2 will pass a molten salt. Both are CoolProp-side, so OPCPFluidArray covers both; the fluid must be a parameter (enum, never a trait object).

BLOCKER TO CHECK BEFORE MOVING: tampines is a PUBLISHED crate, so this is a cross-crate decision for the maintainer, not an agent's. Confirm tampines can reach SolidColumn (currently in tuas_boussinesq_solver) without creating a dependency edge the workspace does not want -- the tampines library is deliberately TUAS-free today, with TUAS only a dev-dependency for its examples.

Composition: OPCPFluidArray (hot fluid) <-> SolidColumn (tube metal) <-> TampinesSteamArray (water/steam), joined by lateral_link_new_temperature_vector_avg_conductance. No temperature cross by construction, since lateral heat flow is evaluated at local node temperatures and simply changes sign rather than violating the second law.
title: Promote the nodalised steam generator into tampines for fhr_sim_v2 reuse
